findings.description: In the requirement loop, `rule_key "$perm"` is called as a bare statement and its return status is not checked. `rule_key` returns 1 for any requirement not shaped `Bash(...)` and, on that path, leaves the global RULE_KEY holding the PREVIOUS iteration's key. The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so if `all_required` ever contains a non-Bash rule the whole checker aborts with exit 1 and no report; if `set -e` is not in effect at that call site (e.g. main invoked in a conditional), the stale RULE_KEY is silently reused and the requirement is classified found/denied based on a different rule. The retired `base_pattern_of` tolerated any string.
findings.failure_mode: Adding a `Read(...)`/`WebFetch(...)`/tool-name requirement to all_required makes every preflight die silently (exit 1, empty output) or misreport that requirement using the prior rule's key.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset `RULE_KEY=""` at the top of rule_key before the shape check, and in main handle the failure explicitly: `if ! rule_key "$perm"; then missing_permissions+=("$perm"); continue; fi` (or warn and skip).

findings.cross_file_justification: The entry's rationale (vendor pricing page: 'Claude 4.6 and later models include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing') applies equally to claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-fable-5 and claude-fable-5-1, which still carry `pricing.long_context` with 2.0×/1.5× multipliers (verified: false). tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py::test_five_family_declares_the_beta_header_list_and_the_long_context_tier pins the tier on FIVE_FAMILY while the new test pins its absence on 5.5, locking in the contradiction.
findings.description: The catalog now encodes two incompatible pricing models for the same vendor family and the same cited source: Opus 5.5 bills >200K-token requests at standard rate, while Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable bill them at 2× input / 1.5× output. One of these is wrong per the cited page. Because metering (calculate_cost_micro / long_context handling) reads this field, cost reports, budget guards and the per-call cost-ceiling test will diverge between `opus` (5.5) and its first fallback hop `claude-opus-5` for identical large-context calls.
findings.failure_mode: A request that falls back from claude-opus-5-5 to claude-opus-5 above 200K input is metered at 2× the cost of the primary hop (or vice versa), producing inconsistent budget accounting and misleading cost tables, and any budget breaker tuned on one model mis-fires on the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the long_context question once from the vendor page and apply it to the whole 4.6+ family: either drop `long_context` from the FIVE_FAMILY entries (and update the two tests), or add it to claude-opus-5-5 with `verified: false` and record in catalog-evidence.md why the vendor statement is not trusted.

findings.description: The defaults change from concrete vendor model ids (`gpt-4o`, `claude-3-opus-20240229`) to catalog aliases (`reviewer`, `opus`). Aliases are only meaningful if every consumer of GPT_MODEL/OPUS_MODEL in this script dispatches through cheval/model-invoke, which resolves them. The section is still labelled 'API configuration' and the prior defaults were raw provider ids, which is the signature of a script that posts `{"model": "$GPT_MODEL"}` directly to a provider endpoint or keys a cost table by model id. The diff does not show the call sites, so this cannot be confirmed from the change itself.
findings.failure_mode: If any call site sends the value to a provider API or a model-id-keyed lookup, the script now fails on every run with a provider `model not found` (HTTP 404/400) or an empty pricing lookup, where it previously worked with the old (if outdated) ids.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify every use of GPT_MODEL/OPUS_MODEL routes through model-invoke/cheval (alias-aware). If a direct curl or id-keyed table remains, resolve the alias first (e.g. via generated-model-maps.sh MODEL_IDS/MODEL_PROVIDERS) or keep concrete ids as defaults.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff writes claude-opus-5-5 with `ceiling_calibration.source: conservative_default`, `calibrated_at: null`, and no `transport`/`method`/`measured_input_tokens`. The HEAD snapshot of this test module supplied for review contains `test_a_foreign_transport_calibration_carries_its_provenance` (asserts `"claude-opus-5-5" in foreign`, method == probed_headless, measured_input_tokens present) and `test_lookup_returns_the_concrete_bound_through_the_gate_path` (asserts 5.5 has `calibrated_at` and ceiling != 180000).
findings.description: The test module and the catalog entry describe mutually exclusive states for claude-opus-5-5. The diff's version of the new test asserts the entry is uncalibrated (conservative_default / calibrated_at None), while other tests in the same module at HEAD assert it is a calibrated, foreign-transport (headless-probed) entry with a measured bound below the 180K cap. Both cannot pass against one catalog. One of the two artifacts in this PR is stale relative to the other.
findings.failure_mode: pytest on `.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py` fails on at least two tests (`'claude-opus-5-5' in foreign` → AssertionError; `calibrated_at` truthiness → AssertionError) against the catalog as shipped in this diff, or, if the catalog is later probed, the diff's own new assertions on `conservative_default` / `calibrated_at is None` fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile within this PR: either ship the probed calibration block for claude-opus-5-5 (transport, method: probed_headless, measured_input_tokens, calibrated_at, matching probed_ceiling/effective_input_ceiling) or remove/guard the two calibrated-5.5 assertions so the module is self-consistent with the uncalibrated entry. Run the module before merge.
